A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PASER. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite renumbering and formatting changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original recovery experiments, including reasoning accuracy, perplexity, code-generation results, ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds knowledge benchmarks, compression settings, a gradient-based comparator, and scalability measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 adds concept normalization, soft down-weighting of uncertain cases, and an optional NLI reranker to the earlier CCG filtering procedure. The clustering, JSD scoring, and budget allocation remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 does not incorporate these enhancements, leaving their experimental use unclear.

E1.justification: v3 adds MMLU and CommonsenseQA knowledge-intensive evaluation in Appendix F and uses xP3x for scalability measurements in Appendix O. The existing Alpaca/LaMini training coverage and language-modeling, reasoning, mathematics, and coding benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix K.3 adds an evaluated LESS-style selector based on embedding-parameter gradient norms. The original comparator sets remain intact. DELIFT, SMART, and Datamodels receive discussion but are not reported as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v3 adds AWQ 4-bit evaluation and recovery after DistiLLM, MiniPLM, or SKD compresses LLaMA2-7B into a 1.5B student. This differs from the retained experiment using distillation to recover already-pruned models. It also adds an xP3x timing experiment with an estimated full-data reference. Existing LoRA schedules and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix O extends the existing component-runtime analysis to extreme-scale xP3x processing, while Appendix K.3 adds efficiency and variability comparisons with gradient-based selection. The original component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity tests, KD/SF combinations, and clustering/CCG case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Table 15 newly reports plus/minus dispersion values for reasoning and perplexity; accompanying text identifies reasoning dispersion as standard deviation. Both versions already specify five runs with different seeds and two-tailed independent t-tests at p < 0.01.

E6.justification: All original table values and plotted results are retained. v3 adds results in Tables 7, 10, 11, and 15, plus xP3x timings, including 65.54 reasoning accuracy under AWQ and 3.21 hours for xP3x selection. These concern additional settings and comparisons. Table 15 contains an apparent erroneous 458.48 reasoning entry, limiting interpretation of that row.

T1.justification: The mathematical method definitions, complexity theorem and proof, and Appendix C's six assumptions, error-bound theorem, and derivation are unchanged apart from notation and formatting.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contribution: capability-aware recovery data selection that improves recovery efficiency using 4%-20% of the original data. The new introductory sentence foregrounds theoretical guarantees already claimed in v2's analysis.

C2.justification: v3 expands the explanation of full-data failure to include capacity constraints, dominant-task overfitting, forgetting, and optimization instability. New Appendix S develops recoverable versus irrecoverable structural damage and attributes weaker Baichuan recovery to specialized, less redundant pathways. These substantially extend v2's brief pruning-quality caveat, although direct architectural evidence is not supplied.

D1.justification: v3 identifies RTX 6000 Ada and H800 hardware where v2 mainly specified GPU memory, documents the xP3x cluster, and describes the new gradient selector. It replaces anonymous code-access instructions with a named GitHub repository and adds a reproducibility statement. Existing principal hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 gains a dedicated data-selection discussion, and new Appendix K extensively positions PASER against LESS, DELIFT, SMART, Datamodels, and related selection approaches. Additional citations support the new benchmarks, compression experiments, and scalability study. This substantially expands the earlier pruning/instruction-tuning positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order remain intact. v3 adds targeted explanations and a question-and-answer appendix, moves the ethics statement forward, removes the NeurIPS checklist, and adds reproducibility, acknowledgments, and expanded LLM-use declarations.

P2.justification: v3 adds four comparison tables, including Table 15's uncertainty and timing columns, and revises some boldface highlighting and captions. The ICLR template changes headers, typography, and placement. All six figure images and the existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added knowledge benchmarks, compression tests, uncertainty reporting, and reproducibility details modestly strengthen empirical support and assessability. Benefits are tempered by Table 15's erroneous 458.48 entry and its claimed 14.2% training-time reduction, which conflicts with approximately 28%-31% from the listed times. The estimated xP3x reference and CCG enhancements without corresponding pseudocode or ablations also limit the gains.
